editor_note: Entry 21 is faithful and reads naturally. "Copiază și salvează bearer token-ul returnat" and "incluzând CRN-ul și bearer token-ul în antetele solicitării" keep both required credentials (CRN and bearer token) in the request headers, and "bearer token" stays in English, as it does in entry 20.

Entry [10] does not translate its source. The English sentence "This example illustrates the DAG by creating a simple circuit that prepares a Bell state…" was replaced by an image embed (![Circuit care pregătește o stare Bell…](…/DAG_circ.avif)). The page loses the sentence that introduces the example and gains a stray, possibly duplicated image, so the entry needs re-translating. There are also minor problems. "Pass" is rendered three ways: "trecere" in [6], a bare English "pass" in [8], and "pas" everywhere else. "Pas" also means "step", which clashes with "acești pași" in [8] and "Pași următori" in [28]. [25] uses the awkward „sandwich-uită" with mismatched quotation marks, and [8] uses the calque "plotare".

examples.source: This example illustrates the DAG by creating a simple circuit that prepares a Bell state and applies an $R_Z$ rotation, depending on the measurement outcome.
examples.translation: ![Circuit care pregătește o stare Bell și aplică o rotație $R_Z$ în funcție de rezultatul măsurătorii.](/docs/images/guides/custom-transpiler-pass/DAG_circ.avif "Circuit")
examples.suggested: Acest exemplu ilustrează DAG-ul prin crearea unui circuit simplu care pregătește o stare Bell și aplică o rotație $R_Z$, în funcție de rezultatul măsurătorii.
examples.why: The entry is an image embed, not a translation of its source. The introductory prose sentence is gone and an image that may be a duplicate is injected instead.

examples.source: create custom transpilation passes … how to write a transpiler pass
examples.translation: treceri de transpilare personalizate … o trecere de transpiler
examples.suggested: pași de transpilare personalizați … un pas de transpiler
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'pas', and [8] even keeps the English 'pass'. Pick one rendering and use it throughout.

examples.source: Before building a pass … To follow these steps … DAG plotting functions
examples.translation: Înainte de a construi un pass … Pentru a urma acești pași … funcțiile de plotare DAG
examples.suggested: Înainte de a construi un pas … funcțiile de desenare a DAG-ului
examples.why: The English word 'pass' is left untranslated, while 'pași' in the same sentence means 'steps', which makes the term ambiguous. 'Plotare' is a calque.

examples.source: Each two-qubit gate is now sandwiched between two Paulis.
examples.translation: Fiecare poartă cu doi qubiți este acum „sandwich-uită" între doi Pauli.
examples.suggested: Fiecare poartă cu doi qubiți este acum încadrată între doi operatori Pauli.
examples.why: 'sandwich-uită' is an awkward coinage, and the quotation marks do not match.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The IDP/SSO explanation in [3], the cost caveat "(poate implica un cost)" in [5] and the dynamic-rules tip in [7] all match the source, and the informal "tu" register holds. Two small things need fixing. In [9], the link text shrank from "App ID documentation" to "[App ID.]", with the sentence's final period moved inside the link. In [6], "Federează utilizatorii tăi la toate produsele" is a stiff calque of "federate … to".

examples.why: The link text shrank to "App ID." and the final period ended up inside the link. The anchor should cover the documentation phrase, as in the English, with the period outside it.

examples.source: Federate your users to all IBM products with IBMid
examples.translation: Federează utilizatorii tăi la toate produsele IBM® cu IBMid
examples.suggested: Federează-ți utilizatorii pentru toate produsele IBM® prin IBMid
examples.why: "Federează … la" copies the English "to" word for word. "pentru … prin IBMid" reads more naturally in Romanian technical prose.

editor_note: Entry 18 is faithful and natural ("Consultă … pentru detalii complete despre clasă"). In entry 25, "nu trebuie instanțiată" is ambiguous in Romanian. It can mean "does not need to be" or "must not be", and in instructional text readers often take it as a prohibition, while the English only says instantiation is unnecessary. "nu este nevoie să fie instanțiată" keeps the optional meaning with no ambiguity. Anyone who reads it as a prohibition would still write correct code, so I'm treating it as a minor wording fix rather than a misleading claim.

examples.source: does not need to be instantiated if you are setting options after initializing the primitive
examples.translation: nu trebuie instanțiată dacă setezi opțiunile după inițializarea primitivei
examples.suggested: nu este nevoie să fie instanțiată dacă setezi opțiunile după inițializarea primitivei
examples.why: "nu trebuie" can be read as "must not", which makes an optional step sound forbidden; "nu este nevoie" keeps the English meaning that it is simply unnecessary.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The pass threshold (at least 16 of 20), the lock after two failed attempts and the Credly data-sharing notice all come through intact, and the informal "tu" register holds. Two phrasing slips remain. In [0], "pentru a-ți testa competențele ... și primești o insignă" breaks the parallel structure: the infinitive purpose clause switches to an indicative verb. In [9], the slash form "pregătit/pregătită" reads like form-filling, not natural prose.

examples.source: to test your quantum diagonalization algorithms skills and receive a badge through Credly
examples.translation: pentru a-ți testa competențele în algoritmi cuantici de diagonalizare și primești o insignă prin Credly
examples.suggested: pentru a-ți testa competențele în algoritmi cuantici de diagonalizare și a primi o insignă prin Credly
examples.why: The purpose clause starts with an infinitive and then switches to an indicative verb, which is ungrammatical. Keep both verbs as infinitives.

examples.source: Make sure you're ready to take the exam.
examples.translation: Asigură-te că ești pregătit/pregătită să susții examenul.
examples.suggested: Asigură-te că te-ai pregătit bine înainte de a susține examenul.
examples.why: The slash form for gender is stiff. A Romanian technical writer would rephrase to avoid it.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and uses the informal "tu" register ("vei începe", "ești pregătit", "informațiile tale"), so nothing here would mislead a learner. In the Credly notice [12], "pentru a asista la administrarea" is a calque of "to assist in": in Romanian "a asista la" usually means "to be present at", so it should be "pentru a ajuta la administrarea". Also in [5], „Run" closes with a straight ASCII quote instead of the Romanian closing quote ”, while [7] uses „…” correctly.

examples.source: to assist in the administration of the IBM Digital Badge program
examples.translation: pentru a asista la administrarea programului IBM Digital Badge
examples.suggested: pentru a ajuta la administrarea programului IBM Digital Badge
examples.why: "A asista la" in Romanian usually means "to attend or witness", so this reads as a calque of English "assist in".
The quote marks don't match: the Romanian opening „ is closed with an ASCII " instead of ”, which is inconsistent with entry [7].

editor_note: I found no semantic drift: the protocol steps, the correction table (01→X, 10→Z, 11→ZX), the U-inverse check and the no-FTL and no-cloning answers all match the English. The main problem is that "quantum state" is rendered throughout with the false friend "stat cuantic" ("stat" means a political state in Romanian). The correct term is "stare cuantică", and the file already uses it in the plural ("stări" in [27], [76], [122], [136]), so the singular and plural don't match. Smaller problems are listed below. "Bit" gets the wrong gender twice ("două biți" in [11] and [53]), and "S-a colaps" in [111] should be "A colapsat". Gate is written both as "Gate" and as "poartă", and [92] has the wrong gender ("acel poartă"). "Consultați" in [35], [47] and [97] slips into the formal register.

examples.source: Alice wants to send an unknown quantum state ... sending him two bits of classical information.
examples.translation: Alice vrea să trimită un stat cuantic necunoscut ... trimițându-i două biți de informație clasică.
examples.suggested: Alice vrea să trimită o stare cuantică necunoscută ... trimițându-i doi biți de informație clasică.
examples.why: 'stat' is a false-friend calque (it means a political state). The correct domain term is 'stare', which the file itself uses in the plural 'stări'. 'Bit' is masculine, so 'doi biți'.
'S-a colaps' is ungrammatical: the verb is 'a colapsa', and it is not reflexive here.

examples.source: we would not use that inverse $U$ gate
examples.translation: nu am folosi acel poartă $U$ invers
examples.suggested: nu am folosi acea poartă $U$ inversă
examples.why: The gender agreement is wrong, and the same sentence also has 'Gate-ului'. [75] uses 'poartă-ul' too, so 'gate' is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: For more on transpilation, see the API reference.
examples.translation: Pentru mai multe informații despre transpilare, consultați [referința API.]
examples.suggested: Pentru mai multe informații despre transpilare, consultă [referința API].
examples.why: This is a formal-register slip. The file otherwise uses informal 'tu', and the same slip appears in [35] and [47].
